newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to seek upgrade from rating agencies.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to seek upgrade from rating agencies.

text.p: Venezuelan government officials hope to persuade rating agencies Standard and Poor's and Moody's Investors Service to upgrade Venezuela in the light of recent reforms, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Thursday.

"We will show them the evolution of the economic program of its future prospects and we will invite them to the country to evaluate the programs in progress with an eye to a reclassification for Venezuela which has been harshly punished (by them) in recent times," Matos told reporters.
"The aim is that hopefully we start the new year in a situation where Venezuela has been reclassified by the risk rating companies," he added.
Venezuela has a long-term foreign currency debt rating of B from S&P's and BA2 from Moody's.
"The conditions are there to ask for a revision," Matos said.
The Venezuelan government launched an IMF-backed economic reform program in mid-April.
